<h2>CDT Weekly Newsletter</h2><br><ul><li><p>EPSRC&nbsp;Postdoctoral Pathway&nbsp;Fellowship&nbsp;-&nbsp;2026&nbsp;Call&nbsp;</p></li><li><p>Storytelling for Research (by yellowlees)</p></li><li><p>Develop Your Research Identity</p></li><li><p>AI &amp; HPC Talk Series &ndash; Autumn 2026</p></li><li><p>AI CDT Lunch and Learn Seminar</p></li><li><p>Bristol Doctoral College (BDC) Events and Opportunities &nbsp;&nbsp;</p></li><li><p>Funding opportunities for Interactive AI CDT students</p></li><li><p>Congratulations!</p></li><li><p>Getting Started at the British Library</p></li></ul><p><p>Welcome to this week's issue of the newsletter.</p></p><br><br><b><p>EPSRC&nbsp;Postdoctoral Pathway&nbsp;Fellowship&nbsp;-&nbsp;2026&nbsp;Call&nbsp;</p></b><br><p><strong data-olk-copy-source="MessageBody">EPSRC&nbsp;Postdoctoral Pathway&nbsp;Fellowship&nbsp;-&nbsp;2026&nbsp;Call</strong>&nbsp;</p>
<p><strong>Closing date: 1 November 2026</strong></p>
<p>Applications are now open for the EPSRC Postdoctoral Pathway Fellowships. These prestigious fellowships offer recent EPSRC-funded PhD graduates&mdash;or those nearing completion of their EPSRC-funded PhD&mdash;the chance to begin their independent research career at the University of Bristol through a two-year funded position. The call is open to both internal and external applicants.&nbsp;</p>
<p>Fellows will have the opportunity to design and lead their own innovative research programme at the cutting edge of Science and Engineering.&nbsp;</p>
<p>Benefits of the Fellowship include:&nbsp;</p>
<ul>
<li><span role="presentation">Working within world-leading research groups at the University of Bristol&nbsp;</span></li>
<li><span role="presentation">Accelerating the transition to independent research&nbsp;</span></li>
<li><span role="presentation">Developing leadership potential in a research context&nbsp;</span></li>
<li><span role="presentation">Establishing&nbsp;a strong foundation&nbsp;for a permanent academic role or future externally funded fellowships&nbsp;</span></li>
</ul>
<p><a title="https://www.bristol.ac.uk/jobs/find/details/?jobId=391221&amp;jobTitle=EPSRC%20Postdoctoral%20Pathway%20Fellow" href="https://www.bristol.ac.uk/jobs/find/details/?jobId=391221&amp;jobTitle=EPSRC%20Postdoctoral%20Pathway%20Fellow" data-auth="NotApplicable" data-outlook-id="2ec22d58-c881-44ef-a00c-995e2ceabe96" data-linkindex="0"><u>Apply through the University jobs portal</u></a>.&nbsp;</p>
<p>Full details, including application guidance and candidate notes, can be found via the link above.&nbsp;</p>
<p>If you have any questions, please&nbsp;contact: <a title="mailto:EPSRC-Postdoctoral-Pathway@bristol.ac.uk" href="mailto:EPSRC-Postdoctoral-Pathway@bristol.ac.uk" data-outlook-id="199f1fef-c686-456e-9620-d11ea313215d" data-linkindex="1"><u>EPSRC-Postdoctoral-Pathway@bristol.ac.uk</u></a>.</p><br><br><b><p>Storytelling for Research (by yellowlees)</p></b><br><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 0cm; line-height: normal; vertical-align: baseline;"><strong><span style="mso-ascii-font-family: Aptos; mso-fareast-font-family: 'Times New Roman'; mso-hansi-font-family: Aptos; color: black; border: none windowtext 1.0pt; mso-border-alt: none windowtext 0cm; padding: 0cm; mso-font-kerning: 0pt; mso-ligatures: none; mso-fareast-language: EN-GB;">Thursday 12 November 2026, 10am - 12:30pm, Room 5.223, Sloane Robinson Building</span></strong></p>
<p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 0cm; line-height: normal; vertical-align: baseline;"><span style="mso-ascii-font-family: Aptos; mso-fareast-font-family: 'Times New Roman'; mso-hansi-font-family: Aptos; mso-bidi-font-family: 'Times New Roman'; color: black; border: none windowtext 1.0pt; mso-border-alt: none windowtext 0cm; padding: 0cm; mso-font-kerning: 0pt; mso-ligatures: none; mso-fareast-language: EN-GB;">How can you help people understand and connect with your research? This workshop explores how imagery, empathy and curiosity can help you engage your audience and communicate the value of your work.</span></p>
<p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 0cm; line-height: normal; vertical-align: baseline;"><span style="mso-ascii-font-family: Aptos; mso-fareast-font-family: 'Times New Roman'; mso-hansi-font-family: Aptos; mso-bidi-font-family: 'Times New Roman'; color: black; border: none windowtext 1.0pt; mso-border-alt: none windowtext 0cm; padding: 0cm; mso-font-kerning: 0pt; mso-ligatures: none; mso-fareast-language: EN-GB;">Combining theory with practical ideas, the session will introduce storytelling tools for researchers, explaining not only how they work but why they are effective.</span></p>
<p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 0cm; line-height: normal; vertical-align: baseline;"><strong><span style="mso-ascii-font-family: Aptos; mso-fareast-font-family: 'Times New Roman'; mso-hansi-font-family: Aptos; mso-bidi-font-family: 'Times New Roman'; color: black; border: none windowtext 1.0pt; mso-border-alt: none windowtext 0cm; padding: 0cm; mso-font-kerning: 0pt; mso-ligatures: none; mso-fareast-language: EN-GB;">The cost is &pound;80 (depending on the number of attendees, with 30 places available). The cost will be charged to your RTSG.</span></strong></p>
<p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 0cm; line-height: normal; vertical-align: baseline;"><span style="mso-ascii-font-family: Aptos; mso-fareast-font-family: 'Times New Roman'; mso-hansi-font-family: Aptos; mso-bidi-font-family: 'Times New Roman'; color: black; border: none windowtext 1.0pt; mso-border-alt: none windowtext 0cm; padding: 0cm; mso-font-kerning: 0pt; mso-ligatures: none; mso-fareast-language: EN-GB;">If you wish to attend, please </span><a href="https://app.onlinesurveys.jisc.ac.uk/s/engineering/sign-up-for-storytelling-for-research-workshop"><span style="mso-ascii-font-family: Aptos; mso-fareast-font-family: 'Times New Roman'; mso-hansi-font-family: Aptos; mso-bidi-font-family: 'Times New Roman'; border: none windowtext 1.0pt; mso-border-alt: none windowtext 0cm; padding: 0cm; mso-font-kerning: 0pt; mso-ligatures: none; mso-fareast-language: EN-GB;">sign up using the online form</span></a><span style="mso-ascii-font-family: Aptos; mso-fareast-font-family: 'Times New Roman'; mso-hansi-font-family: Aptos; mso-bidi-font-family: 'Times New Roman'; color: black; border: none windowtext 1.0pt; mso-border-alt: none windowtext 0cm; padding: 0cm; mso-font-kerning: 0pt; mso-ligatures: none; mso-fareast-language: EN-GB;"> and </span><a href="mailto:proai-cdt-admin@bristol.ac.uk">let us know</a><span style="mso-ascii-font-family: Aptos; mso-fareast-font-family: 'Times New Roman'; mso-hansi-font-family: Aptos; mso-bidi-font-family: 'Times New Roman'; color: black; border: none windowtext 1.0pt; mso-border-alt: none windowtext 0cm; padding: 0cm; mso-font-kerning: 0pt; mso-ligatures: none; mso-fareast-language: EN-GB;">.</span></p><br><br><b><p>Develop Your Research Identity</p></b><br><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 0cm; line-height: normal;"><strong>Tuesday 10 November 2026, 1 - 2pm,&nbsp;</strong><a href="https://teams.microsoft.com/meet/311300892431564?p=goVpAAlepY6WsrMI6f">Online (Microsoft Teams)</a></p>
<p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 0cm; line-height: normal;">Join Pui Anantrasirichai and Steven Ramsay for a session aimed at researchers in the early stages of their academic careers, including those who have recently completed their PhD.</p>
<p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 0cm; line-height: normal;">Drawing on their own experiences, they will share practical advice on establishing a research profile, creating opportunities and finding your place within the research community.</p>
<p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 0cm; line-height: normal;">The talk will be followed by a Q&amp;A.</p>
<p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 0cm; line-height: normal;">If you have topics you would like to see covered in a future How-To Session, or would like to contribute to a session, please email <a href="mailto:cs-staff-enquiries@bristol.ac.uk">cs-staff-enquiries@bristol.ac.uk</a>.</p>
<p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 0cm; line-height: normal;">&nbsp;</p><br><br><b><p>AI &amp; HPC Talk Series &ndash; Autumn 2026</p></b><br><p class="MsoNormal">The AI &amp; HPC Talk Series brings people together to share experiences of using AI and high-performance computing (HPC), including the good, the bad and the ugly, to help others avoid hours of trial and error.</p>
<p class="MsoNormal"><strong>Upcoming talks</strong></p>
<ul style="margin-top: 0cm;" type="disc">
<li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"><strong>Wednesday 28 October, 3.30pm &ndash; Physics G12, Mott Lecture Theatre</strong><br>Huw Day (SEMT): <em>A Crash Course in Federated Learning: Training Centralised Models on Decentralised Data</em></li>

<li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"><strong>Wednesday 25 November, 3pm &ndash; Physics 3.21, Berry Lecture Theatre</strong><br>Jeff Clark and Elena Fillola Mayoral (Chemistry): <em>Using AI to Model Atmospheric Transport for Greenhouse Gases: ML Emulators and Vibe-Coded Simulators</em></li>
<li class="MsoNormal" style="mso-list: l0 level1 lfo1; tab-stops: list 36.0pt;"><strong>Wednesday 9 December, 3pm &ndash; Physics G12, Mott Lecture Theatre</strong><br>Sanne Terry (BriCS): <em>Navigating HPC at Bristol: Resources, Allocations and Support</em>, with an open forum for user feedback.</li>
</ul>

<p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 0cm; line-height: normal; background: white; vertical-align: baseline;"><strong><span style="color: black; mso-color-alt: windowtext;">3. Expressing Criticality in Your Writing</span></strong></p>
<p class="MsoNormal" style="line-height: normal; background: white; vertical-align: baseline; margin: 0cm 0cm 0cm 14.2pt;"><strong><span style="color: black; mso-color-alt: windowtext;">3 November 2026, 14:00&ndash;16:00, Senate House (PGR Hub)</span></strong></p>
<p class="MsoNormal" style="line-height: normal; background: white; vertical-align: baseline; margin: 0cm 0cm 0cm 14.2pt;"><span style="color: black; mso-color-alt: windowtext;">Want to develop your doctoral writing skills? Explore how to critically analyse research, develop your academic voice and use effective writing techniques to communicate your engagement with the literature in this workshop.</span></p>
<p class="MsoNormal" style="line-height: normal; background: white; vertical-align: baseline; margin: 0cm 0cm 0cm 14.2pt;"><span style="color: black; mso-color-alt: windowtext;"><a href="https://www.bristol.ac.uk/doctoral-college/events/#event=78450452;instance=20261103140000?popup=1&amp;lang=en-UK">Book your tickets here</a>.</span></p>
<p class="MsoNormal" style="line-height: normal; background: white; vertical-align: baseline; margin: 0cm 0cm 0cm 14.2pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p class="MsoNormal" style="text-indent: -14.2pt; line-height: normal; background: white; vertical-align: baseline; margin: 0cm 0cm 0cm 14.2pt;"><strong><span style="color: black; mso-color-alt: windowtext;">4. How to Get Published in Research Journals</span></strong></p>
<p class="MsoNormal" style="line-height: normal; background: white; vertical-align: baseline; margin: 0cm 0cm 0cm 14.2pt;"><strong><span style="color: black; mso-color-alt: windowtext;">4 November 2026, 14:00&ndash;16:00, Senate House (PGR Hub)</span></strong></p>
<p class="MsoNormal" style="line-height: normal; background: white; vertical-align: baseline; margin: 0cm 0cm 0cm 14.2pt;"><span style="color: black; mso-color-alt: windowtext;">Want to publish your research but not sure where to start? Join this workshop led by Sharon Harris, Journals Development Editor at University of Bristol Press, who has over 25 years&rsquo; experience in journal publishing. Learn how to choose a suitable journal, understand the editorial and peer-review process, and improve your chances of publication. </span></p>
<p class="MsoNormal" style="line-height: normal; background: white; vertical-align: baseline; margin: 0cm 0cm 0cm 14.2pt;"><span style="color: black; mso-color-alt: windowtext;"><a href="https://www.bristol.ac.uk/doctoral-college/events/#event=78448405;instance=20261104140000?popup=1&amp;lang=en-UK">Book your tickets here</a>.</span></p><br><br><b><p>Funding opportunities for Interactive AI CDT students</p></b><br><p class="MsoNormal">Two additional funding opportunities are available to support&nbsp;<strong>current and former Interactive AI CDT</strong> students.</p>
<p class="MsoNormal"><strong>1. Interactive AI Impact Funding</strong></p>
<p class="MsoNormal">Funding is available to help current and former IAI CDT students explore opportunities to create impact from their PhD research. This could include developing research collaborations, exploring commercial opportunities, informing policy or professional practice, improving public services, supporting communities or contributing to sustainability and public engagement.</p>
<p class="MsoNormal">Support could include travel to collaborators or partner sites, equipment for a pilot project, justified project expenses or up to three additional months of stipend. Most applications are expected to be below &pound;5,000, although larger requests may be considered.</p>
<p class="MsoNormal">The scheme does not cover routine PhD costs, thesis completion or general conference attendance. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the funding is spent.</p>
<p class="MsoNormal"><a href="https://forms.cloud.microsoft/e/nQWTnmmgDL">Find out more and apply</a>.</p>
<p class="MsoNormal"><strong>2. Post-Submission Conference Funding</strong></p>
<p class="MsoNormal">Additional funding is available for IAI CDT students to present papers arising from their PhD at leading conferences after submitting their thesis. Funding can contribute towards registration, travel, accommodation and reasonable subsistence costs.</p>
<p class="MsoNormal">This is separate from RTSG support and is intended for presenting an accepted paper, rather than conference attendance alone. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, subject to available funding.</p>
<p class="MsoNormal"><a href="https://forms.cloud.microsoft/e/u0QEPK02sd">Find out more and apply</a>.</p><br><br><b><p>Congratulations!</p></b><br><p>Many congratulations to Dr Ellie Prosser for winning one of the FSE Best Doctoral Thesis awards this year with a thesis entitled "Interactive Agents for Online Child Safety". <p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 0cm; line-height: normal;">New to the British Library?
